```{r}
#| label: setup-display
#| include: false

# Display-only render: reads saved tables and figures. Nothing is recomputed.
# Set TRUE to re-run the analysis commands in Code & Provenance.
run_analysis <- FALSE

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(tidyverse)
  library(glue)
  library(knitr)
  library(DT)
})

wkdir <- "/resnick/groups/mthomson/jboktor/WILDRxSPF_brains"
base_tag <- "2026-10-06"   # base integrated run (MAST, pseudobulk, D-SPIN, popAlign; class-level pySCENIC)
new_tag  <- "2026-10-07"   # multi-level pySCENIC update + high-level analyses
tbl_dir  <- file.path(wkdir, "tables/SN_Integrated", glue("run_{base_tag}"))
new_dir  <- file.path(wkdir, "tables/SN_Integrated", glue("run_{new_tag}"))
int_dir  <- file.path(wkdir, "data/interim/sn_integrated", glue("run_{base_tag}"))
new_int  <- file.path(wkdir, "data/interim/sn_integrated", glue("run_{new_tag}"))
fig_dir  <- file.path(wkdir, "figures/SN_Integrated", glue("run_{new_tag}"))
pa_tbl   <- file.path(wkdir, "tables/popAlign/snRNASeq/run_2026-10-04_synth-2026-10-05")

rd <- function(f, dir = tbl_dir) { p <- file.path(dir, f); if (file.exists(p)) read_csv(p, show_col_types = FALSE) else NULL }
rn <- function(f) rd(f, new_dir)
not_computed <- function(what) cat(glue("::: {{.callout-warning}}\n**{what} not yet computed** — set `run_analysis <- TRUE` and run the cells in Code & Provenance.\n:::"), "\n\n")
# Embed a saved figure by its path relative to notebooks/ (keeps lightbox + embedding), or say it is missing
show_fig <- function(name) {
  if (file.exists(file.path(fig_dir, name))) cat(glue("![](../figures/SN_Integrated/run_{new_tag}/{name})"), "\n\n") else not_computed(name)
}
dt_table <- function(df, caption, page = 10) {
  datatable(df, rownames = FALSE, filter = "top", class = "compact stripe hover", extensions = "Buttons", caption = caption,
            options = list(pageLength = page, lengthMenu = unique(c(page, 25, 50, nrow(df))), dom = "Bfrtip",
                           buttons = list("colvis", "csv"), scrollX = TRUE))
}
pct <- function(x, d = 0) paste0(formatC(100 * x, format = "f", digits = d), "%")
fmt <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",")
sig2 <- function(x) format(signif(x, 2), scientific = abs(x) < 1e-3)

# ── base run ──
gb   <- rd("integrated_gene_bridge.csv")
pbu  <- rd("integrated_pseudobulk_unit_summary.csv")
pbc  <- rd("integrated_pseudobulk_component_summary.csv")
het  <- rd("integrated_heterogeneity_summary.csv")
dval <- rd("integrated_dspin_validation.csv")
leads_pa <- rd("popAlign_followup_leads.csv", pa_tbl)
pa_cat <- rd("popAlign_subpopulation_catalog.csv", pa_tbl)
harm <- readRDS(file.path(wkdir, "data/interim/sn_integration/sn_harmonized_results_2026-10-06_r2.rds"))
pg <- readRDS(file.path(int_dir, "pseudobulk_unit_genes.rds"))
# ── multi-level pySCENIC update ──
circ  <- rn("integrated_circuit_enrichment.csv")
loao  <- rn("integrated_animal_loao_prediction.csv")
coup  <- rn("integrated_animal_coupling.csv")
sn_u  <- rn("integrated_scenic_native_unit.csv")
sn_c  <- rn("integrated_scenic_native_component.csv")
sn_b  <- rn("integrated_gene_bridge_scenic_native.csv")
sn_l  <- rn("integrated_evidence_leads_scenic_native.csv")
es    <- rn("integrated_effect_size_summary.csv")
conc  <- rn("integrated_unit_concordance.csv")
sizes <- rn("integrated_unit_size_dependence.csv")
nullg <- read_csv(file.path(new_int, "effect_size_permutation_null.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
scen_lvl <- read_csv(file.path(wkdir, "tables/SCENIC/SCENIC_level_summary_display_2026-10-06.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)

# ── headline numbers (all computed from the saved results) ──
gbu <- gb %>% distinct(unit_id, shifted_feature, .keep_all = TRUE)
gb_ok <- gbu %>% filter(!is.na(mast_dirz_shift), !is.na(mast_dirz_control))
z_shift <- median(gb_ok$mast_dirz_shift); z_ctrl <- median(gb_ok$mast_dirz_control)
p_gb <- wilcox.test(gb_ok$mast_dirz_shift, gb_ok$mast_dirz_control, paired = TRUE)$p.value
agree_shift <- mean(gb_ok$mast_dirz_shift > 0); agree_ctrl <- mean(gb_ok$mast_dirz_control > 0)
dsp_shift <- mean(gbu$dspin_any_responsive_overlap_shift, na.rm = TRUE); dsp_ctrl <- mean(gbu$dspin_any_responsive_overlap_control, na.rm = TRUE)

mast_files <- function(u) { p <- str_split(u, "__")[[1]]; file.path(wkdir, "data/interim/mast/snRNASeq/supertype_label", glue("{p[3]}_{p[2]}_2026-01-04.rds")) }
mast_all <- map_dfr(unique(pg$unit_id), function(u) { f <- mast_files(u); if (!file.exists(f)) return(NULL)
  readRDS(f) %>% as_tibble() %>% transmute(unit_id = u, gene = sub("-GRCm39$", "", primerid), coef, mast_padj = p_adjust) })
mj <- inner_join(mast_all, pg, by = c("unit_id", "gene"))
mdeg <- mj %>% filter(mast_padj < 0.1); mbg <- mj %>% filter(mast_padj >= 0.5)
n_mast_deg <- nrow(mdeg)
deg_same <- mean(sign(mdeg$logFC) == sign(mdeg$coef)); bg_same <- mean(sign(mbg$logFC) == sign(mbg$coef))
deg_nom <- mean(mdeg$p < 0.05); bg_nom <- mean(mbg$p < 0.05); deg_fdr <- sum(mdeg$padj < 0.1)
pb_fdr_genes <- sum(pg$padj < 0.1); pb_fdr_units <- n_distinct(pg$unit_id[pg$padj < 0.1]); r_pb <- mean(pg$p < 0.05)

hs <- harm %>% filter(method == "pySCENIC"); n_scen_nuc <- sum(hs$p_adj < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE); r_scen_nuc <- mean(hs$p_adj < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)
hd <- harm %>% filter(method == "DSPIN"); r_dsp <- mean(hd$p_value < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)
r_pa <- mean(pa_cat$p_state < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)
scen_grn <- sum(scen_lvl$GRNs); scen_tests <- sum(scen_lvl$Tests); scen_nom <- sum(scen_lvl$`p < 0.05`) / scen_tests
scen_glob <- sum(scen_lvl$`FDR < 0.10 (global)`)
n_unit_grn <- sum(!is.na(sn_u$n_regulons))

pcs <- pbc %>% left_join(gb %>% distinct(unit_id, comp, p_state), by = c("unit_id", "comp"))
ex_shift <- pcs$excess_p01[pcs$robust & coalesce(pcs$p_state < 0.05, FALSE)]
ex_other <- pcs$excess_p01[pcs$robust & !coalesce(pcs$p_state < 0.05, FALSE)]
p_ex <- wilcox.test(ex_shift, ex_other)$p.value
n_het_units <- sum(het$n_het_fdr10 > 0)
frac_val <- mean(dval$rho > 0, na.rm = TRUE); rho_mast_pb <- median(pbu$rho_mast_pb, na.rm = TRUE)

# native-GRN pySCENIC per subpopulation
snc <- sn_c %>% mutate(grp = case_when(!robust ~ "nonrobust", coalesce(p_state < 0.05, FALSE) ~ "shifted", TRUE ~ "other"))
sc_ratio <- snc %>% group_by(grp) %>% summarise(r = sum(n_p05) / sum(perm_mean), n = n(), .groups = "drop")
scr <- function(g, col = "r") sc_ratio[[col]][sc_ratio$grp == g]
p_sc_shift <- wilcox.test(p_perm_count ~ grp == "shifted", data = snc %>% filter(robust))$p.value
n_comp <- nrow(snc); n_comp_p05 <- sum(snc$p_perm_count < 0.05); n_comp_fdr <- sum(p.adjust(snc$p_perm_count, "BH") < 0.1)
snb <- sn_b %>% distinct(unit_id, shifted_feature, .keep_all = TRUE)
tk_s <- sum(snb$native_enriched_shifted_shift, na.rm = TRUE); tn_s <- sum(snb$native_enriched_tested_shift, na.rm = TRUE)
tk_c <- sum(snb$native_enriched_shifted_control, na.rm = TRUE); tn_c <- sum(snb$native_enriched_tested_control, na.rm = TRUE)
p_tk <- fisher.test(matrix(c(tk_s, tn_s - tk_s, tk_c, tn_c - tk_c), 2))$p.value
nat3_s <- mean(snb$native_n_enriched_shift >= 3, na.rm = TRUE); nat3_c <- mean(snb$native_n_enriched_control >= 3, na.rm = TRUE)
top_tf <- names(sort(table(snb$native_top_shift), decreasing = TRUE))[1:3]

# global effect-size test (exact animal relabelling)
E <- function(m, col, t = "Both") es[[col]][es$method == m & es$tissue == t]
p_all <- E("Pseudobulk: all genes", "p_perm"); p_popa <- E("popAlign programs", "p_perm")
p_dsp <- E("D-SPIN programs", "p_perm"); p_scn <- E("pySCENIC regulons", "p_perm")
p_mdeg <- E("Pseudobulk: MAST DEGs", "p_perm"); r_mdeg <- E("Pseudobulk: MAST DEGs", "ratio_perm")
rank_obs <- nullg %>% filter(method == "Pseudobulk: all genes") %>% group_by(tissue) %>%
  summarise(rank = sum(mean_g2 >= mean_g2[observed]), n = n(), .groups = "drop")
rk <- function(t) rank_obs$rank[rank_obs$tissue == t]
mde_g <- round(power.t.test(n = 6, power = 0.8)$delta, 1)
n_g08 <- ceiling(power.t.test(delta = 0.8, power = 0.8)$n); n_g05 <- ceiling(power.t.test(delta = 0.5, power = 0.8)$n)
n_g08_gw <- ceiling(power.t.test(delta = 0.8, power = 0.8, sig.level = 1e-4)$n)

# circuit + animal-level
C <- function(mod, col) circ[[col]][circ$modality == mod]
pa_auc_hyp <- loao$auc[loao$tissue == "HYP" & loao$scope == "network" & loao$modality == "popAlign"]
pa_p_hyp <- loao$p_one_sided[loao$tissue == "HYP" & loao$scope == "network" & loao$modality == "popAlign"]
scen_loao_max <- max(loao$auc[loao$modality == "pySCENIC"])
cp_core <- coup %>% filter(!str_detect(m1, "^VR"), !str_detect(m2, "^VR"))
coup_net <- median(cp_core$rho_within[cp_core$scope == "network"]); coup_oth <- median(cp_core$rho_within[cp_core$scope == "other"])
K <- function(a, b, col = "rho_partial") { r <- conc %>% filter((str_detect(m1, a) & str_detect(m2, b)) | (str_detect(m1, b) & str_detect(m2, a))); r[[col]][1] }
SZ <- function(m) sizes$rho_size[str_detect(sizes$modality, m)][1]

# ── integrated support for each popAlign lead (pySCENIC now from the GRN fitted on the unit's own nuclei) ──
lead_ev <- leads_pa %>%
  dplyr::select(tissue, lineage, level, name, unit_id, comp, effect, p, depth_flag) %>%
  left_join(gb %>% distinct(unit_id, comp, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
              dplyr::select(unit_id, comp, mast_dirz_shift, dspin_best_resp_p_shift), by = c("unit_id", "comp")) %>%
  left_join(pbc %>% dplyr::select(unit_id, comp, pb_excess = excess_p01), by = c("unit_id", "comp")) %>%
  left_join(sn_l %>% dplyr::select(unit_id, comp, reg_n = comp_n_regulons, reg_hit = comp_n_p05, reg_exp = comp_perm_mean,
                                   reg_p = comp_p_perm, top_regulons), by = c("unit_id", "comp")) %>%
  mutate(mast_ok = coalesce(mast_dirz_shift >= 2, FALSE),
         dspin_ok = coalesce(dspin_best_resp_p_shift < 0.05, FALSE),
         pb_ok = coalesce(pb_excess >= 1.5, FALSE),
         reg_ok = coalesce(reg_p < 0.05, FALSE),
         support = mast_ok + dspin_ok + pb_ok + reg_ok,
         # parenthesised: in R, `!` binds more loosely than `+`
         available = (!is.na(mast_dirz_shift)) + (!is.na(dspin_best_resp_p_shift)) + (!is.na(pb_excess)) + (!is.na(reg_p))) %>%
  arrange(desc(support), desc(support / available), p)
n_leads_multi <- sum(lead_ev$support >= 2); n_leads_mast <- sum(lead_ev$mast_ok); n_leads_reg <- sum(lead_ev$reg_ok)
```

## Overview

**Bottom line.** The four methods measure the same per-animal differences, and once pySCENIC is
refitted on each cell type's own nuclei it agrees with the other three as well. Tested against
every way of splitting the 12 animals into two groups of 6, **no method finds more
WildR vs SPF difference than a random split of the same animals produces.** For whole-transcriptome
expression, the real split ranks near the bottom of the 924 possible splits. Most variation between
animals runs along a hidden axis that crosses the microbiome groups, and every method sees it. The
popAlign network result is still not reproduced by any other method. Earlier evidence that MAST's
DEGs "hold up per animal" was circular: those genes were chosen using the same animals.

::: {.stat-row}
::: {.stat}
[p = `r sig2(p_all)`]{.stat-value}
[WildR vs SPF across all genes, against 924 random animal splits]{.stat-label}
:::
::: {.stat}
[`r fmt(n_scen_nuc)` → `r scen_glob`]{.stat-value}
[pySCENIC regulon hits: nuclei (class GRNs) → animals (`r scen_grn` GRNs, global FDR)]{.stat-label}
:::
::: {.stat}
[`r round(C("popAlign state", "ratio_adj"), 1)`× vs `r round(C("pySCENIC regulons (supertype GRN)", "ratio_adj"), 2)`×]{.stat-value}
[network concentration: popAlign state vs pySCENIC (own GRN)]{.stat-label}
:::
::: {.stat}
[`r n_leads_multi` / `r nrow(lead_ev)`]{.stat-value}
[popAlign leads with support from ≥ 2 other readouts]{.stat-label}
:::
:::

### What we learned

1. **The methods agree on what moves.** popAlign's moving programs carry the MAST signal
   (`r pct(agree_shift)` vs `r pct(agree_ctrl)` of control programs, p = `r sig2(p_gb)`). Refitted
   per cell type, pySCENIC now agrees too: subpopulations popAlign flags carry
   `r round(scr("shifted"), 2)`× the regulon shifts expected from relabelling, against
   `r round(scr("other"), 2)`× elsewhere (p = `r sig2(p_sc_shift)`). This is agreement on the same
   animals, not replication. ([Figures 1–2](#sec-bridge))
2. **There is no global WildR vs SPF signal at the animal level.** For each method we measured how
   far the groups sit apart across all its tests (mean squared effect size) and compared that with
   all 924 ways to split the animals 6 / 6. The real split is unremarkable for popAlign
   (p = `r sig2(p_popa)`), D-SPIN (p = `r sig2(p_dsp)`), pySCENIC (p = `r sig2(p_scn)`) and all
   expressed genes (p = `r sig2(p_all)`). ([Figure 4](#sec-global))
3. **Most variation follows a hidden structure among the animals.** The random splits that separate
   animals most always put 3 WildR and 3 SPF on each side. Every method ranks the splits the same
   way (ρ = 0.55–0.76). The same pairs of animals group together in both tissues, so this looks like
   a property of the animals (cohort, litter, cage or processing day), not of dissection.
   ([Figure 5](#sec-hidden))
4. **The network concentration is still popAlign-only.** Even with networks fitted per supertype,
   pySCENIC shows `r round(C("pySCENIC regulons (supertype GRN)", "ratio_adj"), 2)`× in network units
   (p = `r sig2(C("pySCENIC regulons (supertype GRN)", "p_adj"))`), against popAlign's
   `r round(C("popAlign state", "ratio_adj"), 1)`×. ([Figure 6](#sec-circuit))
5. **Lead priorities.** **HYP PVHd-DMH Lhx6 GABA** is the only lead where popAlign, MAST, D-SPIN and
   pySCENIC all agree (3 of 4 other readouts; pseudobulk excess does not). `r n_leads_reg` leads gain pySCENIC support from their own networks. Because
   every method uses the same 12 animals, this ranks leads for validation; it does not establish an
   effect. ([Table 3](#sec-leads))

### How we got there

- **One scaffold.** Each of the 244 popAlign units (tissue × Allen class / subclass / supertype) is
  linked nucleus by nucleus to MAST, D-SPIN (139 supertypes) and, new here, **the pySCENIC GRN fitted
  on exactly that unit's nuclei** (`r n_unit_grn` / 244 units; the base run used the parent class
  GRN for every unit).
- **Bridges.** Genes (do other methods see the program popAlign sees moving?), cells (per animal ×
  subpopulation pseudobulk and regulon activity), animals (leave-one-animal-out scores) and circuit
  (network enrichment for every method).
- **New global tests.**
  - *Exact animal relabelling:* every method's effect sizes are compared with all 924 relabellings,
    applied jointly to every unit of a tissue. This keeps the correlation between genes, programs
    and units, and assumes no distribution.
  - *Unit concordance:* do the methods agree on *which* cell types carry signal, adjusted for size?

### What to do next

1. **Look for the hidden animal factor.** Check cohort, litter, cage, sex, age, dissection or
   processing date against the groupings in [Figure 5](#sec-hidden) (for example SPF_6 and SPF_9
   vs SPF_3D4 and WildR_10). If it can be identified, adding it as a covariate is the cheapest way
   to gain power.
2. **Plan more animals before more methods.** At 6 per group, only effects of g ≈ `r mde_g` are
   reliably detectable. g = 0.8 needs about `r n_g08` animals per group for one pre-specified test
   and about `r n_g08_gw` at transcriptome-wide thresholds.
3. **Validate the top lead independently** (seqFISH), starting with PVHd-DMH Lhx6 GABA. Score its
   moving program and regulons per animal and region.
4. **Do not use MAST DEG counts or nucleus-level regulon hits as evidence** of a microbiome effect.

## Background

Four analyses of the same WildR vs SPF single-nucleus data had produced four very different
pictures:

- **MAST:** thousands of DEGs;
- **pySCENIC:** hundreds of differential regulons;
- **D-SPIN:** program responses with no animal-level significance;
- **popAlign:** stable composition and a sub-threshold state signal concentrated in one circuit.

They differ in what they test (genes, regulons, programs, subpopulations) and, critically, in what
they treat as a replicate. MAST and the original pySCENIC test count nuclei; D-SPIN and popAlign
count animals. This notebook asks which differences reflect biology and which reflect statistics.

**What changed in this update (`r new_tag`).**

- pySCENIC was refitted at class (36), subclass (137) and supertype (364) level and tested per
  animal ([0X_SCENIC_pySCENIC.qmd]{.path}). Every popAlign unit is now linked to its own GRN.
- All pySCENIC readouts (gene bridge, subpopulation activity, circuit, leave-one-animal-out, leads)
  were recomputed with those GRNs.
- Three high-level analyses were added: an exact global test per method, unit-level concordance,
  and the hidden animal structure.

Method inputs are documented in [0X_Integrated-Results_SN.qmd]{.path}. The plan is
[analysis_md/integrated_analysis_plan.md]{.path}.

## Results

### The methods describe the same expression changes {#sec-bridge}

::: {.figure-card .fig-wide}
```{r}
#| label: show-fig-bridge
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
show_fig("integrated_fig1_gene_bridge.png")
```

::: {.fig-caption}
[**Figure 1.**]{.fig-num} Gene-level bridge. For each robust, uncontaminated popAlign
subpopulation, we compared the oNMF program that moves most between WildR and SPF with the program
that moves least (a control from the same subpopulation and nuclei). (A) Do each program's top 50
genes shift the same way in MAST? Signed z of the mean MAST coefficient against random gene sets,
one point per unit × program (`r nrow(gb_ok)` programs); paired Wilcoxon, moving vs control.
(B) The share of subpopulations whose program is also seen by each other method. "Own GRN" means
the pySCENIC network fitted on that unit's nuclei.
:::

::: {.takeaways}
**Key takeaways**

- **popAlign and MAST see the same shifts.** Median z = `r round(z_shift, 1)` for the moving program
  vs `r round(z_ctrl, 1)` for the control (p = `r sig2(p_gb)`). The agreement is strongest at
  supertype level.
- **D-SPIN partly sees them** (`r pct(dsp_shift)` vs `r pct(dsp_ctrl)`).
- **Unit-specific GRNs make pySCENIC more informative, but not about upstream regulators.**
  - With its own network, a unit's moving and control programs are equally often targeted by ≥ 3
    regulons (`r pct(nat3_s)` vs `r pct(nat3_c)`). Broad regulons still dominate
    (*`r paste(top_tf, collapse = ", ")`*).
  - However, the regulons that target the moving program shift per animal more often
    (`r tk_s` / `r fmt(tn_s)`, `r pct(tk_s / tn_s, 1)`) than those targeting the control
    (`r tk_c` / `r fmt(tn_c)`, `r pct(tk_c / tn_c, 1)`; Fisher p = `r sig2(p_tk)`).
:::

:::

### pySCENIC, refitted per cell type, follows popAlign's subpopulations {#sec-scenic}

::: {.figure-card .fig-wide}
```{r}
#| label: show-fig-scenic
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
show_fig("integrated_fig5_scenic_subpopulations.png")
```

::: {.fig-caption}
[**Figure 2.**]{.fig-num} Regulon activity per animal within each popAlign subpopulation, from the
GRN fitted on that unit's nuclei (`r fmt(n_comp)` subpopulations with ≥ 4 animals per group,
≥ 5 nuclei each). (A) Regulons at pooled-t p < 0.05, divided by the number expected under exact
relabelling of that subpopulation's animals. Bootstrap 95% CI over subpopulations. (B) Distribution
of the per-subpopulation permutation p; the diagonal is chance. (C) Of the regulons whose targets
are enriched in a component's moving (or control) program, the share that shift per animal in that
subpopulation.
:::

::: {.takeaways}
**Key takeaways**

- **Overall, regulon activity per subpopulation is at chance:** `r n_comp_p05` of `r fmt(n_comp)`
  subpopulations at p < 0.05 (≈ `r round(0.05 * n_comp)` expected), `r n_comp_fdr` at FDR < 0.1.
- **But it is concentrated where popAlign sees states move:** `r round(scr("shifted"), 2)`× the
  permutation expectation in state-shifted subpopulations (n = `r scr("shifted", "n")`), against
  `r round(scr("other"), 2)`× in other robust ones (p = `r sig2(p_sc_shift)`). The pattern holds at
  subclass and supertype level. Class-level GRNs, which pool many cell types, missed it.
- **Read this as agreement, not confirmation.** Subpopulations were flagged using these same 12
  animals, and regulon AUC is computed from the same expression. Any difference between the groups
  in these animals, real or not, shows up in both. The test that can tell the two apart is
  [Figure 4](#sec-global).
:::

### Animal-level re-tests: small effects, none resolvable alone {#sec-animal}

```{r}
#| label: tbl-calibration
#| echo: false
tibble(
  Method = c("MAST", "pySCENIC", "D-SPIN", "popAlign (state)", "Pseudobulk (this notebook)"),
  `Original replicate` = c("nuclei", "nuclei", "animals", "animals", "animals"),
  `Original result` = c(glue("{fmt(n_mast_deg)} DEGs in these supertypes (padj < 0.1)"),
                        glue("{fmt(n_scen_nuc)} regulon tests padj < 0.05 ({pct(r_scen_nuc)}; class-level GRNs)"),
                        "245 'star' programs (all WildR animals same sign)",
                        "no shift at FDR < 0.1",
                        "—"),
  `Tested with animals as replicates` = c(
    glue("{pct(deg_nom)} p < 0.05 (non-DE genes: {pct(bg_nom, 1)}); {deg_fdr} at FDR < 0.1 — selected on the same animals"),
    glue("{pct(scen_nom, 1)} of {fmt(scen_tests)} regulon tests p < 0.05 across {scen_grn} GRNs (chance 5%); {scen_glob} at global FDR < 0.1"),
    glue("{pct(r_dsp, 1)} of programs p < 0.05; 0 at FDR < 0.1"),
    glue("{pct(r_pa, 1)} of state tests p < 0.05 (chance 5%); 0 at FDR < 0.1"),
    glue("{pct(r_pb, 1)} of genes p < 0.05; {pb_fdr_genes} genes at FDR < 0.1 ({pb_fdr_units} units)")),
  `Exact relabelling test (Fig. 6)` = c(glue("not testable (circular); all genes p = {sig2(p_all)}"), glue("p = {sig2(p_scn)}"),
                                        glue("p = {sig2(p_dsp)}"), glue("p = {sig2(p_popa)}"), glue("p = {sig2(p_all)}"))
) %>% kable(format = "html", escape = TRUE,
            caption = "How each method's WildR vs SPF result holds up when animals, not nuclei, are the replicates. MAST, pseudobulk, D-SPIN and the relabelling tests: supertype units (6 vs 6). pySCENIC: all 536 testable GRNs at three levels. popAlign: all levels.")
```

::: {.figure-card .fig-wide}
```{r}
#| label: show-fig-animal-de
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
show_fig("integrated_fig2_animal_level_de.png")
```

::: {.fig-caption}
[**Figure 3.**]{.fig-num} (A) Every MAST DEG (padj < 0.1), re-tested by pseudobulk: counts summed
per animal, limma-voom, 6 vs 6. Comparison: genes MAST calls clearly not DE (padj ≥ 0.5) in the same
units. (B) Animal-level DE per popAlign subpopulation (pseudobulk per animal × subpopulation): the
observed share of genes at p < 0.01 divided by 1%. (C) Does the microbiome effect differ between
subpopulations of the same supertype? (limma interaction, animal as a blocking factor). Values near
1 mean no more heterogeneity than chance.
:::

::: {.takeaways}
**Key takeaways**

- **MAST's DEGs keep their direction per animal** (`r pct(deg_same)`), and `r pct(deg_nom)` reach
  nominal p < 0.05, against `r pct(bg_nom, 1)` of non-DE genes. None survives FDR.
- **That enrichment is not independent evidence (correction to the previous version).** The DEGs
  were chosen by MAST using the true labels on the same animals' nuclei. A gene that differs between
  these 12 animals for any reason is both called by MAST and nominally significant per animal. The
  valid test is whether *all* genes separate the groups more than random splits do, and they do not
  (p = `r sig2(p_all)`, [Figure 4](#sec-global)). The same caveat applies to (B): flagged
  subpopulations were selected on the same animals.
- **No evidence that effects are confined to one subpopulation.** Only `r n_het_units` of
  `r nrow(het)` supertypes have any gene with a subpopulation-specific effect, about chance, so
  supertype-level analyses lose little by ignoring substructure.
:::

[Source: cell `cell-run`](#cell-run){.provenance} · tables:
[integrated_pseudobulk_unit_summary.csv]{.path}, [integrated_heterogeneity_summary.csv]{.path}
:::

### No method separates WildR from SPF better than a random split of the animals {#sec-global}

The tests above ask, one feature at a time, whether WildR and SPF differ. Here the question is
global: **across everything a method measures, do the true labels separate the animals more than
labels assigned at random?** The statistic is the mean squared effect size (Hedges g²) over all of a
method's tests in a tissue. The null is all 924 ways to split that tissue's 12 animals 6 / 6, applied
jointly to every unit. This is exact, keeps every correlation, and no gene or unit is selected using
the labels.

::: {.figure-card .fig-wide}
```{r}
#| label: show-fig-global
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
show_fig("integrated_fig6_effect_sizes_power.png")
```

::: {.fig-caption}
[**Figure 4.**]{.fig-num} (A) |Hedges g| of every animal-level test at supertype level (6 vs 6),
per method; grey is the no-effect distribution. MAST DEGs are shown for contrast. They are shifted
because they were selected on these animals. (B) Mean g² for each of the 924 splits of a tissue's
animals (histogram) and for the real WildR / SPF split (line); p = share of splits at least as
large. (C) Power of a two-sample test on per-animal values, by animals per group, for single tests
(solid) and transcriptome-wide thresholds (dotted).
:::

::: {.takeaways}
**Key takeaways**

- **Every method's effect-size distribution matches the no-effect curve** (A). Mean g² sits at or
  just below its permutation mean for pseudobulk (all genes), popAlign, D-SPIN and pySCENIC.
- **The real split is unremarkable, and for expression it is unusually small** (B). Across all genes
  it ranks `r rk("AMY")` of 924 in AMY and `r rk("HYP")` of 924 in HYP, counting from the largest.
  Most random splits separate the animals *more* than the microbiome does. That can only happen if
  the animals differ systematically along some other axis ([Figure 5](#sec-hidden)).
- **MAST DEGs look `r round(r_mdeg, 1)`× "enriched" (p = `r sig2(p_mdeg)`)** only because of
  selection (A): this is what choosing genes on the same animals produces.
- **What 6 animals per group can see** (C): effects of g ≈ `r mde_g` at 80% power for a single
  test. g = 0.8 needs about `r n_g08` per group (one test) or `r n_g08_gw` (transcriptome-wide);
  g = 0.5 needs about `r n_g05` for one test.
:::

[Source: cell `cell-run-update`](#cell-run-update){.provenance} · tables: [integrated_effect_size_summary.csv]{.path}, [integrated_power_curves.csv]{.path}
:::

```{r}
#| label: tbl-effects
#| echo: false
if (!is.null(es)) es %>% filter(tissue == "Both", method != "Pseudobulk: other genes") %>%
  transmute(Method = method, Tests = n_tests, Units = n_units, `Median |g|` = round(median_abs_g, 2),
            `Share p < 0.05` = pct(share_p05, 1), `Mean g² observed` = round(obs_g2, 3),
            `Mean g² relabelling` = round(perm_g2, 3), `Permutation p` = signif(p_perm, 2),
            `Valid test?` = if_else(method == "Pseudobulk: MAST DEGs", "no — genes selected on these animals", "yes")) %>%
  kable(format = "html", caption = "Global relabelling test per method (supertype units, 6 vs 6, both tissues; tissues combined over 10,000 random pairs of per-tissue relabellings).")
```

### A hidden structure among the animals dominates {#sec-hidden}

::: {.figure-card .fig-wide}
```{r}
#| label: show-fig-hidden
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
show_fig("integrated_fig8_hidden_animal_structure.png")
```

::: {.fig-caption}
[**Figure 5.**]{.fig-num} (A) Of the 46 random 6 / 6 splits (top 5%) with the largest
whole-transcriptome separation, how often each pair of animals lands on the same side. Animals are
ordered by clustering. (B) Agreement between methods on which of the 924 splits separate the
animals most (Spearman ρ with pseudobulk).
:::

::: {.takeaways}
**Key takeaways**

- **Animals form groups that cut across microbiome status.** The splits that separate animals most
  are always 3 WildR + 3 SPF per side. The microbiome split is close to orthogonal to them, which is
  why it ranks so low in [Figure 4B](#sec-global).
- **The same structure appears in both tissues.** For example, SPF_6 and SPF_9 group together and
  apart from SPF_3D4 and WildR_10 in both AMY and HYP. That points to a property of the animal
  (cohort, litter, cage, age, sex, processing day) rather than the dissection. The "D4" animals
  (SPF_1D4, SPF_3D4, WildR_3D4) fall together in HYP.
- **Every method sees it** (ρ = 0.55–0.76 with pseudobulk). This is the shared animal-to-animal
  variation in [Figure 8B](#sec-animals): large, consistent across methods, and unrelated to the
  microbiome.
- **Why it matters:** it is the largest source of variance in the data. If its cause is identified
  and recorded, modelling it would sharpen every WildR vs SPF test. If it is a processing variable,
  the balanced design has protected the microbiome comparison from it.
:::

[Source: cell `cell-run-update`](#cell-run-update){.provenance} · data: [data/interim/sn_integrated/run_`r new_tag`/effect_size_permutation_null.csv]{.path}
:::

### The network pattern is not shared by the other methods {#sec-circuit}

::: {.figure-card .fig-wide}
```{r}
#| label: show-fig-circuit
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
show_fig("integrated_fig3_circuit_by_modality.png")
```

::: {.fig-caption}
[**Figure 6.**]{.fig-num} For each method, the share of a unit's tests with p < 0.05 (MAST:
padj < 0.1), compared between MeA → BST → medial hypothalamus network units and all other units.
The ratio comes from a quasi-binomial model on hit counts adjusted for unit size and tissue, with a
95% CI. Supertype units, except "own GRN, all levels", which uses all 244 popAlign units with level
in the permutation strata. The network definition is as in the popAlign report.
:::

::: {.takeaways}
**Key takeaways**

- **Only popAlign state shifts concentrate in the network**
  (`r round(C("popAlign state", "ratio_adj"), 1)`×, p = `r sig2(C("popAlign state", "p_adj"))`).
- **pySCENIC does not, whichever GRN is used:**
  - class GRN `r round(C("pySCENIC regulons (class GRN)", "ratio_adj"), 2)`×;
  - supertype GRN `r round(C("pySCENIC regulons (supertype GRN)", "ratio_adj"), 2)`×;
  - own GRN at all levels `r round(C("pySCENIC regulons (own GRN, all levels)", "ratio_adj"), 2)`×.

  All are non-significant. That class networks were too coarse to see a network effect is therefore
  unlikely.
- **D-SPIN** (`r round(C("D-SPIN programs", "ratio_adj"), 2)`×) and **pseudobulk**
  (`r round(C("Pseudobulk expression", "ratio_adj"), 2)`×) do not concentrate either. MAST finds
  fewer DEGs in network units because they are smaller.
- **Interpretation:** the network result remains a popAlign observation, possibly a population-level
  state change only popAlign is sensitive to, possibly model-specific. It needs an independent
  modality.
:::

### Do methods agree on which cell types carry signal? {#sec-concord}

::: {.figure-card .fig-wide}
```{r}

```

::: {.fig-caption}
[**Figure 7.**]{.fig-num} (A) Spearman correlation between methods of each supertype's hit rate
(share of tests at p < 0.05; MAST padj < 0.1). Ranks are adjusted for log nuclei and tissue;
permutation p within tissue (5,000). (B) Correlation of each method's hit rate with unit size.
:::

::: {.takeaways}
**Key takeaways**

- **The animal-level methods partly agree on which supertypes look different**: pseudobulk–pySCENIC
  ρ = `r round(K("Pseudobulk", "pySCENIC"), 2)`, pseudobulk–D-SPIN
  ρ = `r round(K("Pseudobulk", "D-SPIN"), 2)`, popAlign–pySCENIC
  ρ = `r round(K("popAlign", "pySCENIC"), 2)` (p = `r sig2(K("popAlign", "pySCENIC", "p_partial"))`).
  These are the cell types where the 12 animals happen to split along the group labels, so this is
  consistent measurement, not a microbiome effect (Figure 4).
- **MAST agrees with none of them** once size is removed. Its hit rate is mostly a function of
  nucleus count (ρ = `r round(SZ("MAST"), 2)`), the signature of nuclei-as-replicates.
- **Animal-level methods find more in small units** (ρ = `r round(SZ("Pseudobulk"), 2)` for
  pseudobulk). Small units have noisier per-animal means, which leaves more room for chance
  alignment with the labels.

### Which leads survive integration {#sec-leads}

Each popAlign lead is scored on four readouts from the same animals:

- **MAST:** do its moving program's genes shift in MAST the same way (z ≥ 2)?
- **D-SPIN:** does the best-matching D-SPIN program respond per animal (p < 0.05)? Supertype only.
- **Pseudobulk:** does the subpopulation show excess animal-level DE (≥ 1.5× chance)? Supertype only.
- **pySCENIC (updated):** do more of its regulons shift per animal than exact relabelling of its
  animals allows (p < 0.05)? This uses the GRN fitted on the lead's own unit, so it is now available
  at every level.

"—" means the readout is not available.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-leads
#| echo: false
tick <- function(ok, avail = TRUE) case_when(!avail ~ "—", ok ~ "✔", TRUE ~ "·")
lead_ev %>%
  transmute(
    `Cell type` = glue("{tissue} · {lineage}"),
    Level = str_to_title(level),
    `popAlign` = glue("{if_else(effect == 'state shift', 'state', 'abundance')}, p = {signif(p, 2)}"),
    MAST = glue("{tick(mast_ok, !is.na(mast_dirz_shift))} (z = {sprintf('%.1f', mast_dirz_shift)})"),
    `D-SPIN` = if_else(is.na(dspin_best_resp_p_shift), "—", glue("{tick(dspin_ok)} (p = {signif(dspin_best_resp_p_shift, 2)})")),
    Pseudobulk = if_else(is.na(pb_excess), "—", glue("{tick(pb_ok)} ({sprintf('%.1f', pb_excess)}×)")),
    pySCENIC = if_else(is.na(reg_p), "—", glue("{tick(reg_ok)} ({reg_hit} vs {round(reg_exp, 1)} exp., p = {signif(reg_p, 2)})")),
    Support = glue("{support} of {available}"),
    QC = if_else(depth_flag, "depth-associated", "clean")) %>%
  kable(format = "html", escape = TRUE,
        caption = "Integrated support for each popAlign lead. ✔ = supported, · = not supported, — = not available. Sorted by support, then popAlign p. pySCENIC: regulons at p < 0.05 in the lead's subpopulation vs the exact-relabelling expectation, own-unit GRN.")
```

::: {.takeaways}
**Key takeaways**

- **HYP PVHd-DMH Lhx6 GABA is the best-supported lead.** popAlign, MAST, the best-matching D-SPIN
  program and now pySCENIC all point the same way: its subpopulation carries about twice the regulon
  shifts expected by relabelling.
- **HYP MEA-BST Lhx6 Sp9, DMH Hmx2 (subclass) and AHN Onecut3 GABA keep strong MAST support.** PVH-SO-PVa
  Otp Glut (subclass) gains pySCENIC support.
- **AMY MEA-BST Lhx6 Nr2e1 GABA, popAlign's former top lead, has little support elsewhere**,
  including from its own supertype GRN.
- **Caveat:** all readouts use the same 12 animals, and the global test (Figure 4) is null. Support
  counts rank leads for independent validation; they do not establish an effect.
:::

```{r}

                                               `Regulons tested` = comp_n_regulons, `p < 0.05` = comp_n_p05,
                                               `Expected (relabelling)` = round(comp_perm_mean, 1), `Permutation p` = signif(comp_p_perm, 2),
                                               `Unit-level GRN p` = signif(unit_p_perm, 2), `Top regulon targeting moving program` = native_top_shift,
                                               `Most-shifted regulons (Hedges g)` = top_regulons),
```

## Synthesis & Discussion

[SYNTHESIS]{.eyebrow}

**The question.** Four methods applied to the same nuclei disagreed about how much the
microbiome changes the amygdala and hypothalamus. Is that disagreement biological or statistical?

**Statistical, and the cleanest test finds no microbiome signal at this sample size.**

- *The methods measure the same thing.* Where they can be compared, they agree. popAlign's moving
  programs carry MAST's signal, and pseudobulk and MAST effect sizes correlate (median
  ρ = `r round(rho_mast_pb, 2)` per unit). Per-animal program scores track D-SPIN
  (`r pct(frac_val)` of programs). Refitted per cell type, pySCENIC regulons shift where popAlign's
  subpopulations shift. None of them contradicts another.
- *What separated them was the replicate.* Counted by nuclei, MAST and the original pySCENIC test
  found thousands of hits. Counted by animals, no method has an excess. Compared with every possible
  6 / 6 split of the animals, the WildR / SPF split separates the groups no more than chance, and
  for whole-transcriptome expression less than most random splits.
- *The dominant variation is between animals, not microbiomes.* A hidden grouping of the animals,
  shared across tissues and methods and balanced across WildR and SPF, explains more variance than
  the microbiome. Its cause is not in the recorded metadata.

**What this means for the earlier conclusions.**

1. **The previous version's "small but real" MAST effects are not supported.** Their per-animal
   enrichment follows from selecting genes on the same animals, and the selection-free test is null.
   MAST gene lists are hypotheses, not findings.
2. **pySCENIC differential regulons should not be used as evidence** of microbiome regulation at any
   level (`r scen_glob` of `r fmt(scen_tests)` animal-level tests at global FDR < 0.1). Per-cell-type
   GRNs are useful as annotation: which regulators act in a subpopulation.
3. **popAlign's network result remains uncorroborated.** It is the only pattern that is specific to
   one set of cell types and that also places held-out hypothalamic animals. It still needs an
   independent modality.
4. **The composition result stands.** No method suggests that cell-type or subpopulation proportions
   change, and population averages do not hide opposing subpopulation changes.

**Where to look first.** HYP PVHd-DMH Lhx6 GABA (popAlign, MAST, D-SPIN and pySCENIC agree), followed by MEA-BST
Lhx6 Sp9, DMH Hmx2 (subclass), AHN Onecut3 GABA and PVH-SO-PVa Otp Glut. All are hypothalamic or
extended-amygdala populations. They are candidates for independent validation, not results.

**Limits.**

- All methods analyse the same 12 animals, so agreement between them shows consistency, not
  replication.
- The relabelling test asks about a *global* excess. A strong effect confined to a few genes or cell
  types would barely move a mean over thousands of tests. The per-feature tests (Table 1) cover that
  case, and they are also null after correction.
- The pySCENIC split for AMY 01 IT-ET Glut at class level covers about half its nuclei. Subclass and
  supertype GRNs use all nuclei.

**Bottom line.** At 6 animals per group, the WildR microbiome produces no animal-level change in
amygdala or hypothalamus expression, programs, regulons or composition that any of four methods can
distinguish from a random split of the animals. Animal-to-animal differences of unknown origin are
larger. Next steps are to identify that factor and to add animals, not methods.

## Next Steps

- **Done:**
  - linked MAST, pySCENIC (class / subclass / supertype GRNs), D-SPIN and popAlign on one scaffold;
  - re-tested every method with animals as replicates;
  - added an exact global relabelling test, unit-level concordance and a scan for hidden animal
    structure.
- **Identify the hidden animal factor.** Compare cohort, litter, cage, age, sex and dissection or
  processing date against [Figure 5](#sec-hidden). If found, add it as a covariate and rerun the
  pseudobulk and relabelling tests (cheap: no upstream refit).
- **Power the next experiment from these numbers.** g = 0.8 needs about `r n_g08` animals per group
  for one pre-specified readout. Pre-specify readouts, for example the PVHd-DMH Lhx6 moving program
  or the popAlign network state score, to avoid transcriptome-wide thresholds.
- **Spatial validation (seqFISH)** of PVHd-DMH Lhx6 GABA, then MEA-BST Lhx6 Sp9, DMH Hmx2 and AHN
  Onecut3 GABA, scored per animal and region.
- **Retire nucleus-level claims.** MAST DEG counts and nucleus-level regulon hits should not be
  reported as microbiome effects. Report pseudobulk or relabelling results alongside them.

# Code & Provenance {.code-appendix}

### Methods at a glance

| Stage | What | Unit | Statistic |
|---|---|---|---|
| Gene bridge | popAlign most- vs least-shifted program → MAST direction (signed z), D-SPIN overlap + response, pySCENIC target enrichment (class GRN; **own GRN** in the update) | 432 robust, uncontaminated components | paired Wilcoxon; hypergeometric (BH within component); Fisher |
| Cell bridge | pseudobulk per animal and per animal × subpopulation (limma-voom); microbiome × subpopulation interaction; **regulon AUC per animal × subpopulation from the unit's own GRN** | 139 supertypes (pseudobulk); 244 units / 820 subpopulations (pySCENIC) | moderated t / F; pooled t + exact relabelling of the hit count |
| Global test | Hedges g² over all tests per method vs all 924 relabellings, applied jointly to every unit of a tissue | 139 supertypes, 6 vs 6 | exact permutation; tissues pooled over 10,000 random pairs |
| Concordance | per-unit hit rate, method vs method, ranks adjusted for log nuclei and tissue | 139 supertypes | partial Spearman; within-tissue permutation (5,000) |
| Hidden structure | co-assignment of animals across the top 5% relabellings by whole-transcriptome g² | 12 animals per tissue | descriptive |
| Animal level | leave-one-animal-out score per method; held-out AUC (one-sided); within-group Spearman | 12 animals per tissue | exact (924); within-group permutation (5,000) |
| Circuit | per-unit hit rate, network vs other | 139 supertypes (244 units for own-GRN, all levels) | quasi-binomial adjusted for size and tissue; stratified permutation |

**Inputs (read only, nothing upstream re-run).**

- *MAST:* per-unit results under `data/interim/mast/snRNASeq/{level}_label/` (2026-01-04).
- *popAlign:* run 2026-10-04, synthesis 2026-10-05.
- *D-SPIN:* `data/interim/dspin/<tissue>__<supertype>/` (fit 2026-08-09).
- *pySCENIC:*
  - class GRNs `data/interim/scenic/by_class/` (base run);
  - subclass and supertype GRNs `data/interim/scenic/by_{subclass,supertype}/`;
  - animal-level tests `tables/SCENIC/SCENIC_animal_level_tests*_2026-10-06.csv`;
  - split permutation `tables/SCENIC/SCENIC_split_permutation_tests_2026-10-07.csv`.
- *VR:* `tables/VR/VR1/VR1_per_animal_scores.csv`.

**Outputs.**

- Base run: [tables/SN_Integrated/run_2026-10-06/]{.path}. The 2026-10-06 figures are kept unchanged.
- This update: [tables/SN_Integrated/run_2026-10-07/]{.path},
  [data/interim/sn_integrated/run_2026-10-07/]{.path} and [figures/SN_Integrated/run_2026-10-07/]{.path}.
- The update writes new versions of `integrated_circuit_enrichment.csv`,
  `integrated_unit_rates.csv`, `integrated_animal_scores.csv`,
  `integrated_animal_loao_prediction.csv` and `integrated_animal_coupling.csv`. They keep the
  base-run rows and replace or add the pySCENIC rows.

**Quality notes.**

1. **Selection on the same animals (new).** A set of features chosen with the true labels (MAST DEGs,
   popAlign-flagged subpopulations) will look enriched in any later test on the same animals, so
   such enrichments are not evidence of effect. Global claims rest on the selection-free relabelling
   test.
2. **Relabelling vs theory.** The permutation mean of g² matches the t-distribution value (0.35 at
   6 vs 6), so the null is calibrated. Observed values below it reflect the hidden animal structure,
   not a miscalibrated test.
3. **pySCENIC nucleus-level p-values** are near zero for nearly every regulon and are not used.
4. **Leave-one-animal-out bias.** Held-out predictions are biased against the true label under the
   null, so prediction is tested one-sided.
5. **Calibrated flags.** "Any of 20–240 tests p < 0.05" is true by chance in most units. Unit and
   subpopulation calls use hit rates, a binomial excess or exact relabelling counts.
6. **Unit size.** Network supertypes are smaller, and power scales with size in opposite directions
   for nucleus- and animal-level methods (Figure 7B). Circuit and concordance analyses adjust for it.
7. **Barcodes.** popAlign and pySCENIC nuclei matched one-to-one for every unit checked. The
   per-subpopulation analysis requires ≥ 5 nuclei per animal and ≥ 4 animals per group.
8. **Substitutions.** MOFA2 and sparse CCA are not installed; rank correlations and
   leave-one-animal-out scores replace them.
